contract.name: detect-speech-segments
contract.summary: Score one 32ms window of 16kHz mono audio for human-speech risk using a real Silero VAD model forward pass.
contract.description: A single-chunk speech-risk scorer: given exactly 512 samples (32ms) of 16kHz mono PCM plus the model's own carried streaming state (a 64-sample audio context and an LSTM (h,c) pair, all optional -- default to a cold start), runs one real Silero VAD (snakers4/silero-vad, MIT) forward pass -- reflect-pad, an STFT-as-Conv1d front end, a 4-layer Conv1d+ReLU encoder, one LSTMCell step, a final Conv1d, and a sigmoid -- and returns a speech probability plus the updated context/state to carry into the next chunk. It does not chunk a whole recording, apply a decision threshold, merge adjacent windows into segments, or decide anything about export/sharing -- that is a caller-owned policy over a stream of these scores (mirrors how classifier.release-gate-evaluate and classification.outcome-resolve keep policy separate from scoring). It does not resample audio, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow. On malformed input it fails closed: status is invalid_input and speech_probability is 1.0 (maximum caution), never a false all-clear.

use_cases.scenario: As an audio operator, I want a quiet or silent window scored with low speech probability, so that a caller's downstream policy can let genuinely quiet audio through.

As an audio operator, I want the model's own streaming context and LSTM state threaded from one window's output into the next window's input, so that scoring a real recording chunk by chunk matches scoring it in one pass.
As an audio operator, I want a window of the wrong length rejected with maximum-caution output rather than silently scored, so that a malformed chunk can never look like verified-safe audio.
As an audio operator, I want a malformed carried-context array rejected even when the new samples are valid, so that a corrupted streaming state can never silently reset to a false all-clear.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies exactly 512 samples of 16kHz mono PCM; context/state_h/state_c are optional and default to a cold start (all zeros) when absent.

postconditions.description: Any malformed samples/context/state_h/state_c yields status=invalid_input and speech_probability=1.0 (never a false all-clear).

Identical (samples, context, state_h, state_c) always yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a probability and updated streaming state in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit audio.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#460, follow-up to #455 (second spec 001 FR-017 agent). Motivated by enricopiovesan/Callweave, which fails closed on external review of field recordings pending local speech detection (README.md / DECISION_RECORD.md D-019) and has already vendored this exact model (models/silero-vad/, MIT, SHA256-pinned) but never wired it into its pipeline. Published generically under audio.* rather than callweave.* so any Traverse app can consume it via registry_ref, the same way Callweave already consumes classifier.release-gate-evaluate.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/audio-detect-speech-segments: 15 #[test] cases (VAD1 header parse, bad-magic rejection, reflect-pad-right correctness, forward-pass finiteness/range/determinism/differs-by-input, context-carries-last-samples, fail-closed on missing/wrong-length samples and on malformed context even with valid samples, context/state threading across two calls, f32-array round-trip, sigmoid bounds) against a synthetic fixture at the model's real fixed dimensions; cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=98.22%, regions=97.48%. Separately verified end to end against the real published ONNX graph (snakers4/silero-vad src/silero_vad/data/silero_vad_16k_op15.onnx) via onnxruntime: extracted intermediate tensors (magnitude spectrogram, each encoder layer) to pin down the exact reflect-pad-right(64) / real-imaginary channel split before writing any Rust, then ran the actual built --features full-model artifact under wasmtime across a chained 6-chunk sequence with context/state threaded exactly as the model's own upstream OnnxWrapper.__call__ does -- output matched the real ONNX model to 4 decimal places on every chunk (0.0017/0.1648/0.7735/0.7455/0.8590/0.1593, both sides identical). Not quantized: per-tensor int8 on the LSTM gates was tested and measurably breaks output (max|probability diff| ~0.9 vs the real graph over a 20-chunk sequence, because hidden state carries quantization error forward across every subsequent chunk) -- shipped as plain float32 instead (~1.2 MB, small enough that quantizing wasn't needed for size anyway). Cross-arch (x86_64 vs aarch64) byte-identity was NOT verified -- no x86_64 host or emulator was available in the authoring environment -- hence risk.determinism_class: model_derived rather than deterministic (spec 024). License: snakers4/silero-vad is MIT, verified directly against the repository's own LICENSE file.

contract.summary: Transform a bounded interleaved signed-16 PCM chunk deterministically.
contract.description: Portable pure signal transformation over supplied PCM samples. Downsampling applies a bounded box-average low-pass before decimation; upsampling uses deterministic linear interpolation. This basic filter is not a studio-grade polyphase resampler and requires acoustic-corpus quality evaluation before recognition-quality claims. It converts one- or two-channel layouts and does not decode containers, read/write artifacts, capture devices, choose models, or know a location or application. Call once per bounded chunk; large recordings must be streamed by the Traverse runtime.

use_cases.scenario: As an audio-processing capability consumer, I want PCM resampled and downmixed to a model profile so that inference receives consistent bounded chunks.

As an audio-processing capability consumer, I want unsupported rates, channel layouts, malformed samples, and resource-exceeding outputs rejected so that the module fails deterministically within its memory budget.

preconditions.description: Interleaved signed-16 samples fit the package's 480,000-sample bound and sample count is divisible by input channel count.
Input and target rates are in 8,000..192,000 Hz and channel counts are one or two.

postconditions.description: The same input yields identical output sample values, frame count, rate, and channel count on every supported target.
Downsampling averages the bounded source interval for each output frame before reducing sample rate; this mitigates aliasing but is not a high-quality polyphase filter.
The output contains no more than 480,000 PCM samples.
All output samples remain within signed-16 range.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded computation; no host, network, filesystem, model, or persistent-state access.

contract.summary: Partition bounded signed-16 PCM chunks into deterministic overlapping windows.
contract.description: Pure window extraction over caller-supplied interleaved PCM samples. Emits zero-padded final windows and source-relative start times. Does not decode media containers, access artifacts/devices, or know an application, species, location, or model. The caller must provide a bounded chunk aligned to the desired window policy.

use_cases.scenario: As an audio-inference consumer, I want a PCM chunk split into overlapping fixed-duration windows so that a compatible model can evaluate each window independently.
As an audio-inference consumer, I want invalid or unaligned duration policies, malformed PCM, and excessive window expansion rejected deterministically so that memory use stays bounded.

preconditions.description: Interleaved signed-16 samples fit the 480,000-sample input limit and sample count is divisible by channel count.
Window and hop durations resolve to an exact positive integer number of frames at the supplied sample rate.

postconditions.description: Windows are ordered, have strictly increasing start offsets, and use the configured hop duration.
A non-final chunk emits only complete windows and consumed_frames tells the caller how many leading frames can be released; remaining frames must be carried forward.
Only a final chunk may emit a partial zero-padded window; valid_frames reports source frames before padding.
The output contains at most 64 windows and 480,000 PCM samples total.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded computation; no host, network, filesystem, model, or persistent-state access.

contract.summary: Evaluate supplied bounded privacy-risk evidence against configurable policy.
contract.description: A detector- and domain-neutral privacy policy capability. It evaluates a caller-supplied bounded integer risk score and evidence-completeness fact; a VAD/speech model or human reviewer supplies those facts separately. Policy controls the action for incomplete evidence and elevated risk. This capability does not analyze audio, run a detector, sanitize media, export assets, or know an application/jurisdiction.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy-policy consumer, I want complete evidence below the configured risk threshold permitted so that safe processing may proceed without embedding a specific detector in the policy.
As a privacy-policy consumer, I want incomplete evidence or elevated risk to follow an explicit configured deny/review action so that missing detector coverage cannot be silently treated as safe.

As a privacy-policy consumer, I want incomplete evidence and elevated risk to follow explicitly configured allow actions when a policy owner chooses them so that this evaluator applies policy without silently inventing defaults.
As a privacy-policy consumer, I want incomplete evidence and elevated risk to follow explicit deny and review actions so that each configured fallback is discoverable and testable.

preconditions.description: The caller supplies a 0..1000 risk score and an explicit evidence-complete fact; neither is inferred by this capability.
The configuration explicitly chooses allow, deny, or review_required for both incomplete and over-threshold cases.

postconditions.description: Incomplete evidence takes precedence; otherwise the configured maximum risk score is applied.
The decision is independent of the model/detector that produced input evidence.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded policy evaluation; no host, network, filesystem, model, or persistent-state access.

contract.name: transcribe-speech
contract.summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass (greedy, English-forced decoding).
contract.description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say'. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong. Does not detect speech presence/absence (see audio.detect-speech-segments for that), translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want spoken audio transcribed to text, so that I can search, summarize, or extract entities from what was said without a separate ASR service.
As a meeting organizer, I want silent or empty audio to come back as an empty transcript rather than a hallucinated guess, so that gaps in a recording don't produce fabricated text.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies up to 480000 (30s) samples of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; fewer than 30s of audio is zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window.

postconditions.description: Empty samples, or audio whose total energy is below a small fixed threshold, yields text="" rather than a hallucinated transcript.
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a text transcript in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input audio.

provenance.author: enricopiovesan
provenance.spec_ref: registry#473, fifth and final model from this session's AI-WASM-model review, following #455/#460/#465/#469 -- fifth spec 001 FR-017 agent (fourth genuinely model_backed one; text.detect-language/#469 correctly did not qualify). Motivated as a natural complement to audio.detect-speech-segments (#460): speech-presence detection is a short step from transcription, and free-text output feeds directly into text.detect-entities (#465) and text.detect-language (#469) as a pipeline.

authoring.test_evidence: capability-src/audio-transcribe-speech: 14 #[test] cases (WHSP1 header parse, malformed-table graceful degradation, GELU/LayerNorm/conv1d/sinusoid-embedding math primitives, BPE detokenize incl. special-id exclusion, empty/silent-input -> empty transcript, full pipeline runs without panicking and is deterministic, run() without full-model feature degrades gracefully) against a small structurally-valid synthetic WHSP1 fixture (the fixture's n_audio_ctx is deliberately NOT a free parameter -- it must equal the fixed DSP front end's real conv-computed 1500 timesteps, a genuine integration bug this test caught before publish); cargo llvm-cov functions=100%, lines=98.46%, regions=98.59%. Separately verified end to end against the real published ONNX graphs (Xenova/whisper-tiny onnx/encoder_model.onnx + onnx/decoder_model.onnx) via a from-scratch pure-numpy encoder+decoder implementation (not just calling onnxruntime): matched the onnxruntime baseline token-for-token on a real 11s speech sample (openai/whisper's own tests/jfk.flac fixture, the famous JFK quote) after fixing a real bug caught this way (a forgotten v_proj.bias in the weight-loading dict, silently defaulting to zero and producing a ~17-magnitude hidden-state divergence, invisible without this independent cross-check). Quantization tested (int8 weights incl. the tied embed_tokens table), not assumed: the full greedy autoregressive loop on the same real audio matched the float32 baseline's transcript exactly except for one comma token -- autoregressive token decisions proved robust to per-weight quantization noise, unlike audio.detect-speech-segments' recurrent Silero VAD (registry#460), where int8 measurably broke the LSTM's output. The compiled --features full-model wasm32-unknown-unknown artifact was run under wasmtime (CLI) on the same real audio (both the full 11s clip and a 1s excerpt): output matched the quantized Python reference exactly, byte for byte. Building this artifact against real 176000-sample audio input also surfaced a real bump-allocator OOM (exit(2)) at the prior 64 MiB shared heap ceiling -- not from this capability's own ~41 MiB of audio/attention scratch buffers, but from the shared JSON parser's Vec<Value> being grown by repeated reallocation for a long input array, with every abandoned smaller buffer staying allocated forever in a bump allocator that never frees. Fixed by raising capability-src/wasi-capability-runtime's shared HEAP_SIZE constant 64 -> 192 MiB (same allocator, same zero-cost-headroom rationale as the prior 16->64 MiB raise for registry#384) -- re-ran the full cargo test suite for text.detect-entities, audio.detect-speech-segments, text.detect-language, and report.translate-fr-semantic after the change to confirm no regression from this shared-crate edit. License: dual-attested -- openai/whisper's own GitHub LICENSE file is MIT (verified directly); the openai/whisper-tiny Hugging Face model card's own metadata (cardData.license) says apache-2.0. Both primary sources, both permissive; logged as-is.

contract.name: transcribe-speech
contract.summary: Transcribe speech to text from 16kHz mono audio using a real Whisper-tiny encoder-decoder transformer forward pass, gated on a Silero VAD speech-presence pre-check so it never hallucinates a transcript for non-speech audio.
contract.description: Runs a real openai/whisper-tiny forward pass -- 80-channel log-mel spectrogram front end, a 2-conv1d/4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer encoder, a 4-layer/384-dim/6-head transformer decoder with causal self-attention and cross-attention to the full encoder output, then greedy (argmax, no beam search) autoregressive decoding seeded with a fixed startoftranscript/English/transcribe/no-timestamps prompt -- an officially-sanctioned, documented minimal decoding path (HF's own generation_config.json ships this exact forced-token configuration for this model). New in 1.1.0: before running the (expensive) encoder/decoder at all, the input is scored by audio.detect-speech-segments' Silero VAD engine (registry#460, reused directly, not duplicated) in its own fixed 512-sample chunks; if no chunk anywhere in the clip clears a speech-probability threshold, the capability returns an empty transcript immediately. This fixes a real, observed failure mode in 1.0.0: Whisper has no notion of 'is this speech at all' and would confidently transcribe non-speech, non-silent audio (a tone, music, noise) as plausible-sounding text -- a synthetic sine wave came back as ' [MUSIC PLAYING]'. True silence was already handled by a cheap energy-threshold check; this closes the gap for non-silent non-speech audio. Not a KV-cached decoder: each step recomputes the full decoder stack over the token sequence so far, which is correctness-first and entirely tractable at this model's scale. Complements audio.detect-speech-segments (registry#460) directly (reuses its engine rather than merely being conceptually related to it): an app that already gates on 'is there speech in this clip' is a short step from 'what did it say', and this capability now performs that same check internally by default. Input is up to 30 seconds (480000 samples) of 16kHz mono PCM, roughly normalized to [-1,1]; shorter clips are zero-padded internally to match Whisper's native fixed processing window (longer audio must be pre-chunked by the caller -- this capability does not chunk or stream). Known, documented limitations: output capped at 224 decoded tokens; English-only (language is forced, not detected -- non-English input transcribes as attempted English, once past the speech-presence gate); greedy single-hypothesis decoding, so exact wording (e.g. punctuation) can differ slightly from a beam-search reference without being wrong; the speech-presence gate is a presence check (any chunk clearing the threshold proceeds), not a duration/coverage measurement, so a clip that is mostly non-speech with one brief speech burst is still fully transcribed. Does not translate, diarize speakers, produce timestamps, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

As a meeting organizer, I want an explicit model_unavailable status rather than a silent empty transcript when the artifact was built without its weight table, so that a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of quietly returning nothing.

Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

License: same as v1.0.0 (dual-attested MIT/Apache-2.0 for Whisper-tiny; MIT for Silero VAD, already recorded on audio.detect-speech-segments).

contract.name: wav-pcm16-decode

authoring.test_evidence: Callweave CI run https://github.com/enricopiovesan/Callweave/actions/runs/34998036296 passed the wave-four WASM smoke suite; Registry cargo llvm-cov CI measures this source crate.

contract.summary: Decode bounded RIFF/WAVE integer PCM16 into interleaved samples.
contract.description: Parses RIFF/WAVE chunks and decodes uncompressed PCM16 mono or stereo data into signed-16 sample arrays. Supports bounded chunks with legal metadata chunks and padding. Does not access the filesystem, fetch artifacts, decode other codec/bit-depth profiles, resample, capture audio, invoke models, or know any application, location, or species.

use_cases.scenario: As an audio-processing consumer, I want a bounded WAV PCM16 artifact decoded into typed samples and source-profile metadata so that portable signal-processing capabilities can run on the same sample representation.
As an audio-processing consumer, I want invalid base64 audio bytes rejected explicitly so that malformed containers cannot be misclassified as decoded audio.

preconditions.description: The base64 WAV request is at most 4,000,000 JSON bytes, the decoded RIFF/WAVE artifact at most 2,000,000 bytes, and output at most 480,000 samples.
The input is uncompressed RIFF/WAVE format-tag 1 PCM16, mono or stereo, with a sample rate from 8,000 to 192,000 Hz.

postconditions.description: Every output sample equals the corresponding signed little-endian 16-bit sample in the WAV data chunk; no resampling or channel conversion occurs.
frame_count times channel_count equals samples_s16 length.
Unsupported or malformed input is rejected with a stable result_class and is never partially decoded.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded computation; no host, network, filesystem, model, or persistent-state access.

contract.summary: Evaluate a generic candidate status against configurable accepted and excluded status sets.
contract.description: Taxonomy-neutral and location-neutral eligibility decision over an opaque candidate reference and status. All status meanings and the unlisted-status fallback are supplied by configuration. It does not discover candidates, know a species/location, query a catalog, rank candidates, or persist a decision.

use_cases.scenario: As a candidate-policy consumer, I want a status included in the configured accepted set to be eligible so that candidate catalogs can share one generic policy evaluator.

As a candidate-policy consumer, I want explicit exclusions to override acceptance and unlisted statuses to follow a configurable fallback so that policy decisions are deterministic and fail closed when desired.
As a candidate-policy consumer, I want an unlisted status to be eligible when the configured fallback says eligible so that catalogs can opt into permissive handling explicitly.

As a candidate-policy consumer, I want an unlisted status to be excluded when the configured fallback says excluded so that a restrictive catalog policy can be expressed without application-specific logic.

preconditions.description: Non-empty candidate identity and status are supplied by the caller.
Accepted and excluded status lists each contain at most 16 non-empty values.

postconditions.description: If a status appears in both lists, explicit exclusion wins.
An unlisted status receives exactly the policy's configured eligible, excluded, or review decision.
No candidate meaning is hard-coded; output includes the supplied policy version.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded policy evaluation; no host, network, filesystem, model, or persistent-state access.

core.authorize is a pure, side-effect-free authorization capability designed for maximum reusability across web, mobile, desktop, edge, and AI-agent runtimes.

It deliberately separates policy definition from policy evaluation. The caller supplies a complete, versioned policy configuration at invocation time (or a compact reference in future extensions). The same WASM binary can therefore enforce RBAC, ABAC, ReBAC-lite, hybrid, or explicit allow/deny rules without recompilation.

Key design principles (Persona-Council reviewed):
- Fail-closed by default (default_effect = deny).
- Fully deterministic: identical inputs always produce identical outputs.
- No host, network, or filesystem access.
- Structured, machine-readable output suitable for audit logs, UI enforcement, and downstream agents.
- Explicit support for multi-tenant isolation, hierarchical roles, time/context conditions, ownership, relationships, high-priority denies, and break-glass overrides.
- Obligations are first-class structured objects (not free-form strings) so callers know exactly what additional steps are required.

The capability never mutates state and never contacts external systems. All decision logic lives inside the supplied policy + the deterministic evaluator.

Known intentional limitations (disclosed):
- The evaluator implements a practical subset of common authorization patterns; it is not a full XACML or Cedar engine.
- Complex boolean expressions inside conditions are limited to a small, safe DSL to keep the WASM footprint and attack surface small.
- Policy size should be kept modest when inlined; very large policy sets should be versioned and referenced externally in future iterations.

use_cases.scenario: As a platform security engineer, I want an admin user with the correct role to be allowed to delete a document so that privileged operations succeed when policy permits them.

evaluation_trace: rule admin-delete matched on role+action+resource.type → allow

use_cases.scenario: As a multi-tenant SaaS developer, I want a user to be denied access to a resource that belongs to a different tenant even if they hold a powerful role, so that tenant isolation is enforced.

evaluation_trace: rule tenant-isolation condition matched → deny (priority 200 wins)

use_cases.scenario: As a collaboration product owner, I want the owner of a resource to always be able to update it, so that ownership rights are respected regardless of role.

evaluation_trace: rule owner-update condition principal.id == resource.owner_id → allow

use_cases.scenario: As a security engineer, I want a high-priority explicit deny to override an allow rule so that a compromised or suspended account cannot exercise privileges.

evaluation_trace: rule suspended-deny matched on principal.attributes.status → deny (priority 300)

use_cases.scenario: As a compliance officer, I want an allow decision to carry structured obligations (require MFA + audit) so that the calling system can enforce additional controls.
As a developer, I want any request that matches no rule to be denied when default_effect is deny, so that the system fails closed.
As a runtime, I want an empty or malformed policy to always produce a deny with a clear reason_code so that invalid configurations cannot open the system.

output_example.reason: Policy contains no rules and default_effect=deny

use_cases.scenario: As an incident responder, I want a break-glass flag to allow a temporary override while still recording that the override was used, so that emergency access is possible but fully auditable.

evaluation_trace: break_glass attribute present and enabled in policy

use_cases.scenario: As a client developer, I want a clear structured denial when the principal object is missing required fields so that I can surface a precise error instead of a generic failure.

principal.description: Caller identity. Missing or empty id is not schema-rejected so the guest can return reason_code invalid_principal (UC-09).

attributes.description: Arbitrary key-value attributes (tenant_id, status, department, clearance, etc.)

action.description: The action being requested (read, write, delete, approve, transfer, invite, ...)

context.description: Request-time attributes (time, ip_risk, device_trust, location, incident_id, ...)

condition.description: Simple safe DSL: {op, left, right} where op is eq|neq|gt|lt|in|contains

policy_hash.description: Deterministic hash of the evaluated policy for audit correlation

action must be a non-empty string
resource.type must be a non-empty string
policy must contain version, mode, default_effect and a rules array

postconditions.description: Exactly one of allow or deny is returned
Identical inputs always produce identical outputs

contract.description:
core.calculate-price is a pure, side-effect-free pricing capability designed for maximum reusability across e-commerce, SaaS billing, booking engines, B2B quoting and subscription systems.

It deliberately separates pricing rules from evaluation. The caller supplies a complete, versioned pricing configuration (currency, rounding mode, discount rules, tax rules) at invocation time. The same WASM binary can therefore enforce completely different commercial models without recompilation.

Key design principles (Persona-Council reviewed):
- Pure arithmetic + rule evaluation only. No external tax or catalog services.
- Fully deterministic: identical inputs always produce identical outputs.
- Fail-closed on invalid quantities, negative prices or malformed configuration.
- Explicit ordering and stacking behaviour for discounts.
- Tax calculated on the post-discount taxable base (configurable).
- Full audit trail: every applied rule, intermediate amounts and a config hash.
- Multi-currency aware with explicit rounding mode.

The capability never mutates state and never contacts external systems. All decision logic lives inside the supplied configuration + the deterministic evaluator.

Known intentional limitations (disclosed):
- Does not fetch live FX rates or remote tax jurisdiction data – those must be resolved by the caller and passed in the configuration or context.
- Complex percentage-of-percentage discount interactions are limited to the ordered stack defined in the config to keep behaviour predictable.
- Not a full CPQ (Configure-Price-Quote) engine; it assumes line items are already selected.

contract.name: consent-purpose-check
contract.summary: Pure, deterministic consent and purpose binding check answering whether supplied consent data allows a requested purpose.
contract.description:
Pure, deterministic decision procedure for consent and purpose binding evaluation (issue #500). Evaluates whether caller-supplied consent records allow a requested processing purpose for a subject under a caller-supplied policy version and evaluation timestamp (now). Never accesses external storage, clocks, connectors, or network.

Matching and evaluation semantics:
- Consents are evaluated in declaration order. The first record whose purpose exactly matches requested_purpose determines the decision and matched_consent_index.
- If status is 'withdrawn', decision is 'deny' with reason_code 'consent_withdrawn'.
- If status is 'denied', decision is 'deny' with reason_code 'consent_denied'.
- If status is 'granted', validity timestamps are evaluated: if granted_at > now or unparseable, fails closed with 'deny' / 'invalid_input'; if expires_at <= now, decision is 'deny' with 'consent_expired'; otherwise 'allow' with 'consent_granted'.
- If no record matches requested_purpose, decision is 'deny' with 'purpose_not_granted'.
- Malformed input fields or timestamps fail closed with 'deny' and 'invalid_input'.
- Scope intersection: v1.0.0 performs exact purpose matching; scope is preserved as metadata without filtering.

subject_id.description: Identifier of the data subject whose consent is being evaluated.

now.description: Current evaluation reference timestamp in ISO-8601 UTC format.

policy_version.description: Version identifier of the governing consent policy.

consents.description: List of recorded consent records for the data subject.

purpose.description: Purpose for which this consent record was established.

granted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when consent was granted, or null if omitted.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when consent expires, or null if indefinite.

scope.description: Optional scopes associated with the consent (preserved metadata in v1.0.0).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason code explaining the decision.

matched_consent_index.description: 0-based index of the consent item in the input array that determined the decision, or null if no consent matched.

use_cases.scenario: As a compliance officer, I want a granted consent for the requested purpose to be allowed, so that lawful processing can proceed.
As a compliance officer, I want a withdrawn consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that processing immediately ceases when consent is rescinded.
As a compliance officer, I want an explicitly denied consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that opt-outs are strictly enforced.
As a compliance officer, I want an expired consent for the requested purpose to be denied, so that processing stops once the validity window closes.
As a compliance officer, I want a request with no matching consent purpose to be denied, so that unauthorized purposes fail closed by default.
As a runtime engineer, I want malformed timestamps to be rejected, so that corrupted inputs fail safely without guessing intent.

side_effects.description: Pure deterministic consent evaluation in memory

contract.name: process-comment
contract.summary: Configurable comment action processor: create/edit/reply/delete/react with policy, mentions, and moderation.
contract.description:
core.process-comment is an enterprise-grade, pure, deterministic capability that implements the business logic layer of a modern commenting system (Slack / Teams / Linear / Notion / GitHub quality).

It is deliberately configuration-driven. The same WASM binary can power:
- Public product feedback widgets
- Internal enterprise collaboration
- Code-review and document annotation
- Customer support threads
- Multi-tenant SaaS commenting

The capability never persists data and never sends notifications. It only decides, validates, normalizes and enriches. Persistence, notification delivery, search indexing and real-time fan-out remain the responsibility of the calling system.

Supported actions (via the `action` discriminator):
- create
- edit
- reply
- delete (soft or hard according to policy)
- react (add / remove emoji reaction)
- resolve / unresolve
- pin / unpin

Key enterprise features (Persona-Council reviewed):
- Full lifecycle coverage in one capability
- First-class mention extraction and validation against allowed principals
- Configurable thread depth, parent existence checks and cycle prevention
- Soft-delete with immutable audit fields
- Multi-tenant isolation via attributes
- Visibility models (public, private, restricted, resource-acl, channel)
- Rich-text sanitisation with configurable allowed marks
- Structured obligations (notify, audit, quarantine, rate-limit, moderate)
- Complete evaluation trace + policy hash for eDiscovery and compliance
- Fail-closed on malformed input or policy violations

The capability is pure: identical inputs always produce identical outputs. No host, network or filesystem access is required or permitted.

contract.name: analyze
contract.summary: Analyze a submitted document into deterministic approval-review fields using simple keyword/heuristic rules.
contract.description: Real, deterministic document approval analysis: genuinely reads the `document` input and derives its fields via simple keyword classification (docType), a two-consecutive-capitalized-word heuristic (parties), and a `$`-prefixed number scan (amounts) -- no model, network, randomness, or host state dependency, matching this capability's original design constraints. This replaces the 1.0.1 release, which was a fixed-output fixture that ignored its input entirely. contract.name: analyze
contract.summary: Analyze a submitted document into deterministic approval-review fields using simple keyword/heuristic rules.
contract.description: Real, deterministic document approval analysis: genuinely reads the `document` input and derives its fields via simple keyword classification (docType), a two-consecutive-capitalized-word heuristic (parties), and a `$`-prefixed number scan (amounts) -- no model, network, randomness, or host state dependency, matching this capability's original design constraints. This replaces 1.1.0, which was genuinely input-dependent but built with std + serde_json targeting wasm32-wasip1 -- that import set (environ_get/environ_sizes_get) fails Traverse's own WasmExecutor ABI whitelist, so it could run under a generic wasmtime host but not through traverse-cli agent execute/serve or an embedder SDK. This version is built no_std on the shared agents/wasi-agent-runtime/ shim: verified to import only wasi_snapshot_preview1::{fd_read, fd_write, proc_exit}, so it is both input-dependent and genuinely executable by Traverse's runtime. Known limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: the party-extraction heuristic is intentionally simple and can false-positive on any two consecutive capitalized words at a sentence start (e.g. "This Agreement"), not just genuine named parties -- acceptable for a reference-tier, no-model capability, not production-grade named-entity recognition. Source: agents/doc-approval-analyze/ in this repo.

use_cases.scenario: As an accounts-payable clerk, I want a submitted invoice to be automatically classified with its party and amount extracted, so that a document with strong signals can move straight to high-confidence approval routing.

As an accounts-payable clerk, I want plain text with no recognizable signals to be flagged as low confidence, so that I know to review it manually instead of trusting an automated read that found nothing.

input_example.document: just some plain lowercase text with no signals

use_cases.scenario: As an accounts-payable clerk, I want a document with only a recognized type but no extracted party or amount to land at medium confidence, so that it's routed for manual review rather than auto-approved on a partial read.

contract.summary: Put, get, or delete a durable approval packet via host managed state.
contract.description: Stateful store for a single approval packet (packet_id, document_id, status, reviewer_ids[]) persisted under the fixed state_schema key `packet` via traverse_host::{state_put,state_get,state_delete}. Resource identity lives inside the value. Does not emit events. Browser targets are excluded.

side_effects.description: Reads and writes host DataStore persistence for key packet via state_get/state_put/state_delete

preconditions.description: action must be one of get, put, delete
put requires packet with non-empty packet_id, document_id, status, and reviewer_ids array

use_cases.scenario: As an approvals manager, I want to put an approval packet into durable store, so that reviewer assignments survive across sessions.
As an approval consumer, I want to get a previously stored approval packet, so that my workflow can render reviewers and status.
As an approvals manager, I want to delete a stored approval packet, so that closed packets do not linger in managed state.
As an approval consumer, I want get to fail closed when no packet exists, so that absent state is explicit.
As an approvals manager, I want put with an incomplete packet rejected, so that partial writes cannot corrupt the store.
As a compliance officer, I want unknown actions rejected, so that clients cannot invent store verbs.

evaluation_trace: action must be get, put, or delete

use_cases.scenario: As a compliance officer, I want host persistence failures surfaced as host_error, so that callers can fail closed when DataStore is unavailable.

contract.summary: Create a bounded append request for an opaque immutable event.
contract.description: Pure event-envelope validation and append planning. It preserves the caller-supplied event payload reference, versioned type, aggregate reference, causal references, timestamp, and idempotency key. A generic event-store connector owns durable append, ordering, and replay behavior. This capability does not persist events or depend on any app/workflow/domain.

use_cases.scenario: As an event producer, I want a validated immutable event envelope shaped into an append request so that different applications can use the same event-store connector.
As an event producer, I want missing identity fields, malformed causal references, and oversized requests rejected before requesting persistence so that the host receives only bounded envelopes.

preconditions.description: Event identity, event type/schema version, aggregate and payload references, occurrence time, and idempotency key are non-empty and bounded.
The causal-reference array contains at most 16 non-empty opaque references.

contract.name: format-currency
contract.summary: Format a numeric amount as a currency display string, with correct decimal places and symbol placement for a disclosed, finite set of currency/locale combinations.
contract.description: Formats amount as a currency string using currency_code's standard minor-unit decimal places and locale's symbol-placement convention, both drawn from a small fixed, disclosed table covering exactly 8 currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, AUD, INR, BHD) and 5 locales (en-US, en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR, ja-JP) -- not a live ISO 4217 registry and not full ICU/CLDR data; see SPEC.md for the exact table. An unrecognized currency_code or locale falls back to a generic '<CODE> <amount>' format rather than guessing, and supported: false is returned so the caller can detect the fallback rather than silently trusting an unstyled result. Negative amounts are formatted with a leading minus sign before the symbol (e.g. '-$12.50'), not locale-specific parenthetical negative notation, in this version.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a finite numeric amount and an ISO 4217 currency_code string.

postconditions.description: formatted is always a non-empty string, even for an unsupported currency_code/locale (generic '<CODE> <amount>' fallback rather than an error).
supported: false whenever either currency_code or locale fell outside this version's disclosed lookup tables and the generic fallback format was used.

side_effects.description: Produces one formatted string derived from the provided amount/currency_code/locale.

contract.name: process
contract.summary: Extract deterministic structured meeting notes from one transcript.
contract.description: Reference app capability for meeting notes that genuinely reads the `transcript` input: scans it line by line (split on newlines/periods) for action-item keywords ("will", "todo", "action item"), decision keywords ("decided", "decision", "agreed"), and follow-up keywords ("follow up", "follow-up", "next step"), heuristically extracting an owner/made_by (the line's leading capitalized word) and a due date (the word following "by") where present. contract.summary: Create a model activation eligibility plan from verified evidence and configurable runtime policy.
contract.description: Pure model-neutral policy planning. Consumes trusted evidence labels from an authorized verifier and explicit target/runtime compatibility and memory facts. It neither verifies signatures or digests nor fetches, selects, downloads, caches, executes, or activates an artifact. Runtime remains responsible for independently enforcing activation authority.

use_cases.scenario: As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want a compatible artifact with verified provenance, accepted licence evidence, and sufficient memory to receive an activation plan so that runtime-specific activation can remain separate from portable policy.

As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want target, memory, failed evidence, and unknown-evidence cases rejected or escalated according to explicit policy so that unsupported or unverifiable artifacts are not silently approved.
As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want failed digest, signature, licence, or compatibility evidence to reject an activation plan so that every negative evidence state is explicit and testable.

As a model-runtime policy consumer, I want unknown signature, licence, and compatibility evidence to follow the configured reject action so that incomplete verification cannot be mistaken for approval.

preconditions.description: Evidence values are supplied by an authorized verifier/runtime; this pure evaluator does not establish their authenticity.
The host runtime independently enforces artifact verification, permissions, and activation. This output is a policy plan, not activation authority.

postconditions.description: Target and memory constraints are checked before evidence; failed evidence rejects and unknown evidence follows explicit review/reject policy.
No model artifact is fetched, selected, cached, executed, or activated.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded policy evaluation.

contract.name: execute
contract.summary: Execute a signed exact-ref model package through traverse.model-runtime (Spec 138).
contract.description: Catalog-facing shim over the traverse.model-runtime connector operation model.execute. Consumers supply an exact-ref model pin (model_id, version, digest), a host-staged input_ref, app-declared model_usage (commercial|non_commercial), and a trust_root of allowed signer key ids. The capability validates those inputs, dispatches via mediated connector_invoke, and surfaces the host's verified model_evidence on success. Fail-closed Spec 138 reasons (digest_mismatch, key_untrusted, signature_invalid, rights_mismatch, rights_policy_denied, usage_undeclared, package_revoked, model_unavailable) pass through unchanged. It does not fetch Hugging Face, hold signing keys, or select a model — the pin is consumer-supplied. The reference package for catalog demos is traverse.digits-onnx@1.0.0 from Traverse fixtures.

use_cases.scenario: As an inference operator, I want a signed exact-ref digits-onnx package executed with declared non_commercial usage so that the host returns verified model_evidence without embedding a model in this capability.
As an inference operator, I want an omitted model_usage rejected with usage_undeclared so that undeclared commercial intent cannot silently proceed.
As an inference operator, I want an empty trust_root rejected with key_untrusted so that unsigned or untrusted packages cannot execute.
As an inference operator, I want a tampered package digest reported as digest_mismatch so that integrity failures stay fail-closed across hosts.
As an inference operator, I want a rights pin mismatch reported as rights_mismatch so that package rights cannot drift from the declared pin.

No signing keys, host paths, or credentials appear in output.

contract.name: collect-fragments
contract.summary: Normalize caller-supplied source fragments into a clean, de-duplicated, order-preserving source_fragments list.
contract.description: First node of the report.* chain, ported from the UMA chapter-13 portable MCP runtime's DataProviderLocal (re-scoped from a canned-fixture provider to a real input normalizer). Genuinely reads the `fragments` input and returns `source_fragments`: each fragment trimmed of surrounding whitespace, empty/whitespace-only fragments dropped, case-insensitive exact duplicates dropped (first occurrence kept), original order preserved, and any fragment longer than 2000 characters clipped on a UTF-8 char boundary. Also returns `dropped_count` (how many input fragments were removed) and `status` (`ok`, or `insufficient_data` when nothing survives normalization). No model, network, randomness, or host state dependency: identical input always produces identical output. Built no_std on the shared capability-src/wasi-capability-runtime shim, verified to import only wasi_snapshot_preview1::{fd_read, fd_write, proc_exit}, so it is genuinely executable by Traverse's runtime ABI whitelist. Known limitation, disclosed rather than hidden: de-duplication is exact-match only (after trim, clip, and lowercase) -- near-duplicate fragments that differ by punctuation or wording are both kept, which is correct for a normalizer that must not lose caller intent. Source: capability-src/report-collect-fragments/ in this repo.

contract.summary: Create a delayed, approval-aware retention action plan without executing it.
contract.description: Pure generic policy planner. Converts an eligibility classification into no action or a configured archive/delete plan with explicit grace period and approval state. It never deletes, archives, reads, or writes assets. The host must re-check holds and references at execution time, require approval when specified, and invoke the separately authorized storage connector.

use_cases.scenario: As a retention steward, I want an eligible asset to receive a delayed archive or deletion plan according to policy so that retention actions are auditable and not immediate side effects.
As a retention steward, I want held or retained assets to produce no action, and eligible plans to fail on time overflow, so that protected data is not scheduled for removal.
As a retention steward, I want an asset already retained under policy to produce no archive or delete plan so that retained data is not actioned a second time.

preconditions.description: retention_state is supplied from a current eligibility evaluation; this capability does not query dependency or hold state.
Evaluation time is an explicit Unix epoch value supplied by the caller; no ambient wall clock is read.

postconditions.description: Held and retained states produce no action regardless of configured eligible_action.
Eligible plans execute no earlier than evaluation_time plus a grace period of at most one year; overflow is rejected.
No storage operation occurs; the host must revalidate eligibility/holds and enforce approval before executing the plan.

side_effects.description: Pure bounded policy planning.

contract.name: detect-entities
contract.summary: Extract named entities (person, organization, location, misc) from free text using a real DistilBERT-NER model forward pass.
contract.description: Runs a real DistilBERT (dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0) token-classification forward pass -- WordPiece tokenize (case-preserving; capitalization is real signal for this model), 6 transformer layers, per-token BIO-tag classification, then merge adjacent B-/I- tags of the same type into entity spans with byte offsets into the input text. Returns an array of {text, label, start, end} (label one of PER, ORG, LOC, MISC; start/end are UTF-8 byte offsets). A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or a 'leading capitalized word' heuristic. Known limitation, faithfully reproduced rather than hidden: this compact model sometimes tags interior WordPieces of a multi-piece entity with a fresh B- tag instead of a continuing I- tag, which this capability's BIO merge (correctly) reports as separate adjacent entities rather than guessing they should be one -- e.g. 'Acme Corp' can come back as three short spans. Does not resolve entities against a knowledge base, deduplicate mentions, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want person, organization, and location entities extracted from a sentence, so that a caller can build a structured summary without a keyword list.

input_example.text: Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want a well-known person, organization, and location correctly grouped into single clean spans when the model tags them consistently, so that common cases read naturally.

input_example.text: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want text with no named entities to return an empty array rather than a forced guess, so that ordinary sentences aren't mislabeled.

input_example.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

use_cases.scenario: As a meeting organizer, I want empty input to return an empty array rather than an error, so that an empty upstream field never breaks the pipeline.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: Each entity's start/end are UTF-8 byte offsets into the exact input text string, and entities[i].text equals input.text[start..end].
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces an entity array in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

contract.name: detect-language
contract.summary: Identify the language of free text using a from-scratch character-trigram frequency classifier trained on 24 languages.
contract.description: Normalizes input text (collapse whitespace, lowercase, pad), extracts its own top-400 character trigrams by frequency, and scores each of 24 trained languages by the integer rank-distance between the text's trigrams and that language's top-300 trigram frequency profile (Cavnar & Trenkle 1994, 'N-Gram-Based Text Categorization') -- a trigram absent from a language's profile costs a fixed max penalty. Returns the lowest-distance language, an integer 0-100 confidence derived from the margin to the second-best language, and the top-3 candidate languages with their raw distances. Input with fewer than 5 distinct trigrams (very short or empty text) returns 'und' (undetermined) rather than a low-confidence guess. Trained on UDHR (Universal Declaration of Human Rights) translations across ar, bg, cs, da, de, el, en, es, fi, fr, he, hi, hu, id, it, ja, nl, pl, pt, ro, ru, sv, ta, uk. Not a port of CLD2 or any other existing language-ID library -- CLD2 was investigated and found impractical to port faithfully (see registry#469) -- this is an original implementation of a well-documented public technique. Does not detect languages outside the trained set, does not handle mixed-language text (scores the whole input as one language), and does not read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a support-ticket router, I want the language of an incoming ticket identified, so that I can route it to the right glossary/locale before further processing.

input_example.text: Bonjour, je n'arrive pas à me connecter à mon compte depuis hier soir et j'ai besoin d'aide rapidement.

use_cases.scenario: As a support-ticket router, I want a clear 'undetermined' result rather than a false guess when there isn't enough text to classify responsibly, so that I don't misroute short or empty input.

input_example.text: ok

language.description: ISO 639-1 code of the detected language, or 'und' if undetermined.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: language is one of the 24 trained ISO 639-1 codes, or 'und' when the normalized input has fewer than 5 distinct character trigrams.
candidates is sorted ascending by distance, ties broken by ascending language code, and its first entry (if present) matches language.

Identical input yields identical output. Every quantity in scoring is a non-negative integer (no floating-point arithmetic anywhere in the hot path), so this is byte-identical across build/host architectures, not just within one WASM instantiation -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a language classification in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

Originally proposed as a CLD2 (Compact Language Detector 2) port; CLD2's own primary source (CLD2Owners/cld2/internal/) was investigated and found impractical to port faithfully (~80+MB of hand-packed, undocumented-format C++ n-gram tables across a dozen+ generated files, multi-stage hashing algorithm, no included offline-generation pipeline). contract.name: redact-entities
contract.summary: Redact person, organization, and location mentions from free text using text.detect-entities' real DistilBERT-NER forward pass.
contract.description: Runs the exact same tokenize -> DistilBERT-NER forward pass -> BIO-decode pipeline as text.detect-entities (registry#465, dslim/distilbert-NER, Apache-2.0), reused directly via a source-level dependency rather than duplicated, then substitutes a bracketed placeholder ("[PER]", "[ORG]", "[LOC]", "[MISC]") for each detected entity span instead of returning raw entity data -- copying everything else through unchanged. A real model forward pass at execution time, not a keyword list or regex-based masking. Second pick (after audio.transcribe-speech@1.1.0's VAD gate, registry#477) from a post-#473 downstream-capability review of this session's shipped model engines: no new model, no new license/verification burden -- same weight table, same license record as text.detect-entities. A new capability id, not a version of text.detect-entities, since "redact" is a genuinely different action from "detect" for a caller (different intent, different output shape), not a refinement of the same one. Inherits text.detect-entities' documented model limitation faithfully: this compact model sometimes tags an interior WordPiece of a multi-piece entity with a fresh B- tag instead of a continuing I-, which the shared BIO merge (correctly) reports as separate adjacent spans -- so a name like 'Acme Corp' can come back partially redacted as '[ORG][ORG][ORG]' rather than one '[ORG]', verified directly against the real model rather than assumed. Does not detect speech, translate, resolve entities against a knowledge base, read storage, invoke connectors, or know an application or workflow.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want person, organization, and location mentions blanked out of a document before it leaves a privacy boundary, so that a forwarded support ticket or shared transcript doesn't carry PII a vendor or auditor shouldn't see.

input_example.text: Sarah Chen from Acme Corp will follow up with the Berlin team next week.

output_example.redacted_text: [PER] from [ORG][ORG][ORG] will follow up with the [LOC] team next week.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want a well-known person and organization consistently redacted even when the model tags them as several adjacent spans, so that no fragment of a detected entity leaks through unredacted.

input_example.text: Elon Musk founded SpaceX in California.

use_cases.scenario: As a privacy export reviewer, I want text with no detected entities returned completely unchanged, so that redaction never alters content that doesn't need it.

input_example.text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

output_example.redacted_text: The quarterly report is due next Friday.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string (may be empty).

postconditions.description: Every byte of the input not covered by a detected entity span appears unchanged, in order, in redacted_text; each detected span is replaced by exactly one bracketed placeholder ([PER]/[ORG]/[LOC]/[MISC]).
Identical input yields identical output within one WASM instantiation. Cross-instantiation / cross-host-architecture byte-identity is NOT proven -- see risk.determinism_class.

side_effects.description: Produces a redacted string in memory; does not log, persist, or transmit input text.

contract.name: truncate
contract.summary: Truncate free text to a caller-supplied Unicode-scalar length budget, with an optional ellipsis included inside that budget.
contract.description: Counts Rust char values (Unicode scalar values), not UTF-8 bytes or grapheme clusters. If text already fits within max_length, returns it unchanged with truncated=false. Otherwise, returns at most max_length Unicode scalars with truncated=true: by default a single Unicode ellipsis (…); when a custom ellipsis is supplied, the ellipsis is included inside the same total budget. If the ellipsis itself is longer than max_length it is clipped to the budget, and max_length=0 returns an empty string. This capability is deterministic, memory-only, and does not interpret HTML, display width, or grapheme clusters.

ellipsis.description: Suffix used when truncation occurs; included inside max_length and clipped if longer than the entire budget.

text.description: Original text when it fits; otherwise a prefix plus the requested ellipsis, with total Unicode-scalar length no greater than max_length.

truncated.description: True exactly when the input text exceeded max_length.

preconditions.description: Caller supplies a text string and a non-negative integer max_length; ellipsis is optional and defaults to ….

When the input text contains at most max_length Unicode scalars, output text equals the input exactly and truncated is false.
When truncation occurs, the selected ellipsis is counted inside max_length; if the ellipsis itself exceeds the budget, only its first max_length Unicode scalars are returned.
Identical input yields identical output using only Unicode-scalar counting and deterministic string slicing; see risk.determinism_class.

contract.name: normalize-phone-number
contract.summary: Normalize a phone number to E.164 format and check its digit-count plausibility for its country code.
contract.description: Strips formatting characters (spaces, dashes, parentheses), determines a calling code (from an explicit leading '+' or from the default_country input), and checks the remaining digit count against a fixed table of plausible national-number lengths for a supported set of country calling codes. Returns the E.164-formatted number when plausible. This is NOT a carrier/HLR lookup and does NOT verify the number is actually assigned, active, or reachable -- it is pure format/plausibility validation, deterministic and offline, using a small disclosed table of supported country codes (see SPEC.md), not the full ITU-T numbering plan database. line_type is always "unknown" in this version since distinguishing mobile/landline/VoIP requires carrier data this capability does not have access to. Known, disclosed limitation: does NOT strip domestic trunk prefixes (e.g. the leading '0' in how a UK or German number is normally written for in-country dialing, such as '020 7946 0958') -- when relying on default_country rather than an explicit '+' prefix, the caller must supply the number already in national-significant-number form (no leading trunk digit), or normalization will report digit_count_implausible for an otherwise-valid domestic-format number.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the phone field, in any common formatting (spaces, dashes, parens, optional leading +).

postconditions.description: When valid: true, e164 is a well-formed E.164 string ('+' followed by 1-15 digits) and country_code/national_number are its decomposition.
Never performs a live carrier/HLR/network lookup -- valid: true means format-plausible for the identified country code, not that the number is assigned or reachable.

side_effects.description: Produces one normalization result derived from the provided phone string; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.

contract.description: Computes a deterministic 0-4 strength score and a human-readable issue list from structural properties only. Exact model: 1 point each for containing a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, a digit, and a symbol (a structural score of 0-4); +1 bonus if the password is at least twice min_length; -1 each for a 4+ character sequential run (e.g. '1234', 'abcd', either direction) and a 4+ character immediate repeat (e.g. 'aaaa'); if the password is shorter than min_length, the whole score is capped at 1 regardless of character diversity (a short password is weak even if varied); if require_symbol is true and no symbol is present, the score is capped at 3. Every unmet criterion and triggered penalty is reported individually in issues (not merged into combined messages). Deliberately does NOT check the password against a known-breached-password list (e.g. HaveIBeenPwned) -- that requires a live network call, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist; a caller wanting breach-checking must do that outside the sandbox, separately, ideally without ever passing the plaintext password to a third-party service uncontrolled by the caller. The password value itself is never included in the output.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the password field, possibly empty.

postconditions.description: score is an integer 0-4; strength is the corresponding label (very_weak, weak, fair, strong, very_strong).
The output never contains the input password value, in whole or in part.
Never checks the password against any external breach/leak database -- structural scoring only.

side_effects.description: Produces one scoring result derived from the provided password; does not log, persist, or transmit the input password.

contract.name: validate-email
contract.summary: Validate whether a string is a syntactically well-formed email address.
contract.description: Checks structural validity of an email address (local-part@domain shape, character classes, length, dot placement) against a simplified, deterministic ruleset -- not full RFC 5321/5322 grammar and not a deliverability check. Does not perform DNS/MX lookups, does not verify the mailbox exists, and does not attempt SMTP verification, since none of those are possible from inside the capability sandbox (no network access) and would be non-deterministic even if they were. Whitespace is not trimmed by this capability -- callers must trim input themselves; a leading/trailing space is treated as an invalid character and reported as such. Plus-addressing (`user+tag@domain`) is treated as valid by default per the `allow_plus_addressing` input field.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the email field, possibly empty.

postconditions.description: Returns valid: true only if the string matches the documented simplified email-shape ruleset; otherwise valid: false with a non-null reason explaining which rule failed.
Never performs DNS/MX/SMTP verification -- valid: true means structurally well-formed, not that the mailbox exists or accepts mail.

side_effects.description: Produces one validation result derived from the provided email string; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.

contract.name: validate-luhn
contract.summary: Check whether a numeric string passes the Luhn checksum, as used by credit card numbers and other identifiers.
contract.description: Applies the standard Luhn (mod 10) checksum algorithm to a digit string: doubling every second digit from the rightmost, subtracting 9 from any result over 9, summing all digits, and checking the total is a multiple of 10. This is a checksum-format check only -- it does NOT verify the number belongs to a real, active account, is not stolen, or is authorized for any transaction (none of that is possible without a live call to a card network or issuer, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist). Luhn validity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for treating a card number as safe to charge. Formatting characters (spaces, dashes) are stripped before checking when strip_formatting is true (the default); the input is never logged, persisted, or included in the output.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the number field, possibly containing spaces/dashes if strip_formatting is true.

postconditions.description: valid: true means the digit string passes the Luhn checksum, nothing more -- not that it is a real, active, or authorized account number.
The output never contains the input number value, in whole or in part.

side_effects.description: Produces one checksum result derived from the provided number; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.

contract.summary: Check whether a numeric string passes the Luhn checksum, as used by credit card numbers and other identifiers.
contract.description: Applies the standard Luhn (mod 10) checksum algorithm to a digit string: doubling every second digit from the rightmost, subtracting 9 from any result over 9, summing all digits, and checking the total is a multiple of 10. This is a checksum-format check only -- it does NOT verify the number belongs to a real, active account, is not stolen, or is authorized for any transaction (none of that is possible without a live call to a card network or issuer, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist). Luhn validity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for treating a card number as safe to charge. Formatting characters (spaces, dashes) are stripped before checking when strip_formatting is true (the default); the input is never logged, persisted, or included in the output.

use_cases.scenario: As a checkout flow developer, I want a well-formed card number with spaces or dashes to still pass the Luhn checksum, so that a customer who types their card number with natural formatting isn't wrongly rejected.
As a checkout flow developer, I want a single mistyped digit to fail the Luhn checksum, so that I can catch an obvious card-number typo before submitting a doomed charge attempt.
As a checkout flow developer, I want an empty string to be rejected before any checksum math runs, so that a blank card-number field fails fast with a clear reason instead of an ambiguous result.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the number field, possibly containing spaces/dashes if strip_formatting is true.

postconditions.description: valid: true means the digit string passes the Luhn checksum, nothing more -- not that it is a real, active, or authorized account number.
The output never contains the input number value, in whole or in part.

side_effects.description: Produces one checksum result derived from the provided number; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.

persona.name: Accounts-Payable Clerk
persona.summary: A company employee who receives and processes incoming vendor documents -- invoices, purchase orders, receipts.
persona.description: The first human touchpoint for a document entering the company's document-approval workflow. Submits a received document to doc-approval.analyze to have its type, party, and amount automatically extracted and confidence-scored, so a well-formed, strongly-signaled document can move straight to approval routing without manual re-keying, while a low-confidence or ambiguous document is flagged for the clerk's own manual review before it goes any further. Does not make the final approve/reject decision -- that's the next role in the workflow.

distinguished_from.how: Handles the initial intake and automated analysis of a document; does not make the approve/escalate decision. The approvals manager is a separate, downstream role in the same workflow that reviews what the clerk's tooling already analyzed.
Processes vendor documents (invoices, purchase orders), not meeting transcripts -- a different internal workflow and a different capability entirely.

Uses doc-approval.recommend to independently recompute a document's approvability from its actual extracted signals, rather than trusting a claimed confidence score at face value -- so a document whose analysis claims high confidence but has no real supporting extracted data gets caught and downgraded instead of silently auto-approved. Never handles the raw incoming document directly; only ever works from documents doc-approval.analyze has already processed.

distinguished_from.how: Reviews and decides on documents the clerk's tooling has already analyzed; does not do the initial intake, submission, or raw-document handling.
Reviews vendor documents for approval, not meeting transcripts -- a different internal workflow and a different capability entirely.

distinguished_from.how: Needs append-only successor revision metadata for immutable artifacts, rather than classifying whether an asset must be retained or is only eligible for later action.

Consumes portable signal-processing outputs rather than preparing evidence bundles for a human review decision.

persona.description: Ensures own_only and role gates prevent cross-user comment mutation. Uses core.process-comment not_owner denials as evidence that edit/delete privileges are enforced.

distinguished_from.how: Focuses on principal ownership/privilege rules, not multi-tenant isolation mechanics.
Owns access-control correctness, not soft-delete retention/eDiscovery obligations.

persona.name: Signup Form Developer
persona.summary: A software developer building the account-creation/registration form for a web or mobile product.
persona.description: Owns the signup experience: validating that an email address is structurally well-formed before creating an account (validation.validate-email), and giving a new user real-time, actionable feedback on password strength so a weak password is caught before the account is created rather than after (validation.score-password-strength). This is specifically the identity/credential-creation step of a product, before any purchase or transaction exists for the user.

distinguished_from.how: Works on account creation, before the user has any purchase intent -- not the payment/shipping flow, which only exists for a user who already has an account.
Works on a product's signup form specifically, not its core note-taking/productivity feature -- a different feature area even if the product happened to be the same app.

persona.name: Summary Consumer
persona.summary: Consumes deterministic bounded-period summaries derived from included and pending references.
persona.description: Uses summary.aggregate to roll included and pending references into one bounded aggregate record with explicit counts, scope identity, and carry-forward facts. Needs deterministic period summaries without embedding visualization, storage, or policy routing into the capability.

distinguished_from.how: Consumes aggregates over references within a bounded scope, rather than finalizing the bounded period record itself.
Needs deterministic aggregate counts and references, rather than converting those counts into an uncertainty score.

persona.name: Support Ticket Router
persona.summary: Routes incoming free-text support tickets to the right locale/glossary/downstream process based on detected language.
persona.description: Receives free text of unknown origin (support tickets, contact-form submissions, chat transcripts) and needs a language classification before further processing -- selecting a glossary, locale-specific templates, or a language-appropriate downstream model. Needs a clear 'undetermined' signal rather than a low-confidence guess when there isn't enough text to classify responsibly, so short or empty submissions don't get silently misrouted.

distinguished_from.how: Needs a language code for one free-text item to pick a routing path, rather than a governed per-item outcome state (provisional/surprising/unknown/rejected) derived from scored evidence and policy thresholds.
Routes text by detected language for downstream processing, rather than configuring blocklists or quarantine obligations for unsafe content.

persona.name: Uncertainty Consumer
persona.summary: Consumes deterministic uncertainty scores derived from aggregate counts and coverage state.
persona.description: Uses uncertainty.score to convert bounded counts, coverage state, and pending-reference facts into one reason-coded uncertainty score. Needs explicit uncertainty that remains tied to supplied evidence boundaries rather than hidden heuristic workflow behavior.

distinguished_from.how: Consumes a scored uncertainty result from aggregate facts, rather than the aggregate facts themselves.
Converts coverage and count facts into a bounded uncertainty score, rather than classifying the completeness state of a coverage window.

persona.name: Visual Composer
persona.summary: Consumes deterministic visual mapping outputs as composition inputs without rendering or storing final artifacts.
persona.description: Uses visual.parameter-map to convert bounded summary and uncertainty facts into stable composition parameters such as density, motion, or palette signals. Needs deterministic mapping inputs for later rendering stages, while keeping rendering and persistence outside the capability boundary.

distinguished_from.how: Consumes visual composition parameters derived from summary facts, rather than the bounded aggregate summary record itself.
Uses uncertainty and summary facts to derive visual parameters, rather than producing the uncertainty score itself.
